name: Shelah
overview: Shelah, the son of Judah, is a significant figure in the genealogical and narrative framework of Genesis and Numbers. Scripture records Shelah as the third son of Judah, born after the deaths of his brothers Er and Onan (Genesis 38:5, 46:12). Judah’s hesitation to give Tamar, his daughter-in-law, to Shelah as a wife reveals the complexities of covenant faithfulness and family responsibility (Genesis 38:11, 14, 26). Furthermore, Shelah’s descendants formed the family of the Shelanites, marking his continuing legacy within the tribe of Judah (Numbers 26:20). These passages highlight Shelah’s role in God’s providential preservation of Judah’s lineage, ultimately pointing toward the Messianic line.
